'''Savas Dimopoulos''' ({{IPAc-en|d|ɪ|ˈ|m|ɒ|p|ə|l|ɒ|s}}; {{langx|el|Σάββας Δημόπουλος}}; born 1952) is a [[particle physicist]] at [[Stanford University]]. He worked at [[CERN]] from 1994 to 1997. Dimopoulos is well known for his work on constructing theories [[beyond the Standard Model]].

==Life==
He was born an ethnic [[Greeks|Greek]] in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]] and later moved to [[Athens]] due to ethnic tensions in Turkey during the 1950s and 1960s.

==Education and career==
Dimopoulos studied as an undergraduate at the [[University of Houston]].  He went to the [[University of Chicago]] and studied under [[Yoichiro Nambu]] for his doctoral studies.  After completing his Ph.D. in 1979, he briefly went to [[Columbia University]] before taking a faculty position at [[Stanford University]] in 1980. During 1981 and 1982 he was also affiliated with the [[University of Michigan]], [[Harvard University]] and the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. From 1994 to 1997 he was on leave from Stanford University and was employed by [[CERN]].

Dimopoulos is well known for his work on constructing theories [[beyond the Standard Model]], which are currently being searched for and tested at [[particle collider]]s like the [[Large Hadron Collider|LHC]] at CERN and at experiments all over the world.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Charitos|first1=Panos|last2=Papageorgiou Koufidou|first2=Athena|title=Interview with Savas Dimopoulos|url=http://ph-news.web.cern.ch/content/interview-savas-dimopoulos|website=PH: Newsletter of the PH department|publisher=CERN|access-date=2015-03-31|archive-date=2016-03-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303221956/http://ph-news.web.cern.ch/content/interview-savas-dimopoulos}}</ref> For example, in 1981 he proposed a [[softly broken]] [[Special unitary group|SU]](5) GUT model with [[Howard Georgi]], which is one of the foundational papers of the [[Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model]] (MSSM). He also proposed the [[ADD model]] of [[large extra dimension]]s with [[Nima Arkani-Hamed]] and [[Gia Dvali]].

==Awards==
In 2006, the [[American Physical Society]] awarded Dimopoulos the [[Sakurai Prize]], "For his creative ideas on dynamical symmetry breaking, [[supersymmetry]], and extra spatial dimensions, which have shaped theoretical research on TeV-scale physics, thereby inspiring a wide range of experiments."<ref>APS Physics, "[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Savas%20Dimopoulos&year=2006 2006 J. J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics Recipient] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719143155/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?name=Savas%20Dimopoulos&year=2006 |date=2018-07-19 }}" (accessed July 21, 2009).</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Faces and places: APS honours particle physicists|journal=CERN Courier|date=June 2006|volume=46|issue=5|page=42|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733932|access-date=2015-03-31|archive-date=2020-06-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615015645/http://cds.cern.ch/record/1733932|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2006, he received the [[Tomassoni awards|Caterina Tomassoni and Felice Pietro Chisesi Prize]] at the University of Rome, Italy. "The prize recognizes and encourages outstanding achievements in physics. Dimopoulos was lauded by the Tomassoni Committee as "one of the leading figures in theoretical particle physics. His proposal of the supersymmetric standard model has aided the understanding of high-energy physics mechanisms."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2006/april26/ppl-042606.html|title=Stanford News Honors and Awards|access-date=June 3, 2014|archive-date=February 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225102304/https://news.stanford.edu/news/2006/april26/ppl-042606.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

He appeared in the 2013 documentary film ''[[Particle Fever]]'', about the work of the [[Large Hadron Collider]].

He is a member of the U. S. [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|title=News from the National Academy of Sciences|date=April 26, 2021|access-date=July 2, 2021|quote=Newly elected members and their affiliations at the time of election are:  ...  Dimopoulos, Savas; Hamamoto Family Professor, department of physics, Stanford University, Stanford, Calif.|archive-date=September 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210923124137/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2021-nas-election.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
